name: Adam Baker

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. This is confidential. Tell me what an ordinary day at the contact centre is like.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and have handled customer calls and chats at this centre for years. I finished secondary school, earn the usual rate, and keep up with the ordinary order and payment queue. I use AI every day to sort long messages, then check the order before I answer. I like trying a useful tool early, but I still put my name on the reply.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner, Sonya, and I have two children in school and a mortgage. She works at a bakery, and we have about four months of expenses saved. There are some other centres within reach. I like helping a new agent learn why a refund failed; I dislike when a clean summary makes a wrong fee look settled.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AI Plateau sounds like my current message sorter: helpful when the thread is long, but the agent still checks the order. I would show a trainee the source page before accepting a neat summary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my job remains and our four-month reserve covers a surprise, though it is not money to throw at gadgets. Sonya’s bakery hours can vary, so the mortgage still asks for both wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep taking calls and using the sorter with the order page open. In the first year of minor change, I’d add the cost of one bought lunch each week to our house reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the budget, calm about the tool. A clean summary is no good if it hides the fee the customer called about.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the sorter miss?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I once found a handling fee in the second half of a chat that the summary skipped. I opened the order, explained the fee and showed the trainee where it sat.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why save lunch money?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Sonya (my partner) and I would keep the reserve for the mortgage and real repairs. Lunch money is small, but it is a number I can move each week.

say: I’d call the **message sorter** helpful only with order checks.
I’d show trainees the **source page** behind a tidy summary.
think: I think my **job remains** in this mild picture.
I still watch **bakery hours** and the mortgage with four months saved.
do: Keep **taking calls** and checking sorted messages in 2026.
Add **lunch money** weekly to the house reserve in the first year.
feel: **Uneasy** about bills, calm about the tool.
S0.quote: A clean summary is no good if it hides the fee the customer called about.
fieldNote: He uses **AI daily** but checks source orders.

He teaches a trainee to find a **missed handling fee**.

steps.text: Keep answering calls and checking sorted messages against orders
Save the cost of one bought lunch weekly for mortgage bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will take the standard chats I answer most days. I would ask for error and paid-hour figures, then test the new reply system before we trust it with a live return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my own hours could shrink even if I know the software, because fewer agents may handle more exceptions. Some nearby centres might offer work, but they may be making the same calculation.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d test the new reply system on twenty old return cases during a paid shift and log wrong fees. In the first year routine chats move, I’d apply for a posted paid billing role only if the offered wage and weekly hours cover our mortgage, while keeping my current job until a signed offer arrives.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, and curious enough to check the numbers. A tool I can use well can still remove the paid calls I use it on.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you test the replies?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare the proposed refund with the receipt and ask another agent to check five cases independently. I would take the corrected counts to my manager, not call a demo proof.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you train for a new role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not pay for a course just because a new screen appears. If a posted paid job requires a funded course on paid time, I would consider it after reading the wage.

say: I’d request **error and paid-hour figures** before trust grows.
I’d test **old returns** before live customers receive new replies.
think: I think my **own hours** could shrink despite tool skill.
I doubt nearby centres offer **certain openings**.
I need a **signed offer** before leaving my current call wage.
do: Test **twenty return cases** with the new system on paid time in 2026.
Seek **posted billing work** at offered mortgage-covering weekly wage and hours in the first year.
S1.quote: A tool I can use well can still remove the paid calls I use it on.
fieldNote: Daily **AI use** does not ensure continued hours.
He keeps his **current wage** until a firm signed paid offer arrives from an actual employer.

steps.text: Test twenty old return cases with the new reply system on paid time
Apply for posted billing work only with offered mortgage-covering weekly wage and hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2028 could handle the whole call, not only the draft. I would ask for written staffing dates and posted paid roles before anyone loses a shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think cheap thinking AI could take most of my headset work in 2028. Robots around 2031 do not help a screen worker, and four months saved cannot keep the mortgage paid through a long search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d defer the planned replacement of our working cooker and put any extra pay into savings. In the first year after 2028, I’d apply for a posted paid service-desk role only if its offered wage and hours cover our mortgage, and take a funded course on paid time only if required for that opening.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed, though I can still prepare. Four months of savings is a short bridge from one pay packet to another.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say about the cooker?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Sonya (my partner) the cooker still works and can wait. If it becomes unsafe, we would fix it; the deferral is only while it is safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make a course real?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for the actual vacancy, the starting hours and who pays the training time. A course with no job at the end is not worth spending our mortgage money.

say: I’d ask for **written dates** and paid roles before cuts.
I’d say **2028 thinking AI** threatens the whole call.
think: I think AGI could take **most headset work** in 2028.
I see **four months saved** as a short bridge.
do: Defer the **working cooker** only while safe and save extra pay in 2026.
Apply for **posted service work** after 2028 with offered mortgage-covering wage and hours.
Take a **funded course** on paid time only if required for that posted paid service opening.
S2.quote: Four months of savings is a short bridge from one pay packet to another.
fieldNote: He sees **2028 thinking AI** as the relevant deadline.
The **cooker deferral** stops if safety changes.
Training needs **funded paid time** for a real posted vacancy.

steps.text: Delay cooker replacement only while the current cooker stays safe
Save any extra shift pay from 2026 for mortgage bills
Apply for posted paid service work with offered mortgage-covering wage and hours after 2028
Take funded course on paid time only if required for the posted paid service opening

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives time to see if checking wrong automated answers is an actual paid role. I would ask for the posted wage and training hours before enrolling anywhere.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could learn quality review in five years, though full AGI might do much of the checking too. I do not want to call a new title safe without a real vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I’d take an employer-funded quality-review course on paid time only if a posted paid role requires it. In the first year after 2031, I’d apply for that role only if its written weekly wage and hours cover our mortgage, keeping current calls until a signed offer arrives.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but I can test the job without rushing. Five years before AGI in 2031 lets me learn a paid role without treating a certificate as a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the course need to teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask a quality agent to show me three wrong refund decisions during the funded course. I want to find the error myself before a customer takes the loss.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Sonya check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show Sonya (my partner) the full week of pay, not only a higher hourly rate. A shorter week at a better rate could still miss the mortgage.

say: I’d ask for **posted wages** before quality training.
I’d ask for **paid study hours** tied to a real role.
think: I think I could learn **quality review** over five years.
I know **full AGI** might do review work too.
do: Take **funded paid-time training** only for a posted review role.
Apply for **posted paid review** after 2031 at written mortgage-covering weekly wage and hours.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to test a paid role.
S3.quote: A shorter week at a better rate could still miss the mortgage.
fieldNote: He wants **real wrong refunds** in the course.
The training needs **funding and paid time** for a posted role.
He compares **whole-week pay** before switching jobs.

steps.text: Take employer-funded quality-review course on paid time only for a posted paid role
Apply for posted review work with written weekly wage and hours covering mortgage after 2031

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives time to strengthen the mortgage reserve and see which posted jobs really pay. I would keep paid first shifts open for new agents to learn beside experienced people.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could keep earning and saving for years, but thinking AI may still take calls in 2036. Robots around 2039 come later, and they do not change the first risk to my headset.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep taking calls and save a fixed amount from each pay. In the first year after 2036, I’d apply for a posted paid customer-service role only if my hours fall and its written wage and hours cover our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the long end, okay about next year. A decade before AGI in 2036 gives me time to save without assuming my headset is permanent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you teach a new agent?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show a new agent how to check a return receipt on a paid shift. My own first supervisor did that, and it is a better start than a list of links.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the family move?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the children at their school unless Sonya (my partner) and I had a signed offer and an affordable route. Some nearby centres mean we can search before moving.

say: I’d defend **paid first shifts** so new agents can learn beside experienced people.
I’d ask for **posted wages** as 2036 approaches.
think: I think I could **earn and save** for years.
I know **2036 thinking AI** could still take calls.
do: Keep **taking calls** and save a fixed amount from each pay.
Seek **posted paid service work** after 2036 if hours fall, only with written mortgage-covering wages and hours.
feel: **Uneasy** about later calls, secure for now.
S4.quote: A decade before AGI in 2036 gives me time to save without assuming my headset is permanent.
fieldNote: He values **paid first shifts** as a way to learn work.
A move needs a **signed offer** and affordable school route.

steps.text: Keep taking calls while the centre staffs them
Save a fixed amount from each pay for the mortgage

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. Knowing today’s tools may not keep my calls paid when cheap thinking AI can handle the whole account. I would need early notice, a posted paid opening with mortgage-covering weekly hours, and funded training during paid time if the job requires it.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who teaches a new agent to question an answer. A new agent needs a paid first shift beside someone who will let them spot a mistake.

headlineQuote: A new agent needs a paid first shift beside someone who will let them spot a mistake.
portrait: At **43**, Adam is an experienced average-skill agent after secondary school on typical pay.
He and Sonya support **two schoolchildren** and a mortgage with four months saved.
He uses **AI daily** but checks orders before sending replies.
He values **paid practice** and real openings as thinking work shifts.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could make his current AI skill insufficient to protect a paid call role.
whatWouldHelp: Early **notice**, posted mortgage-covering work and required funded training on paid time would help.
